title: The Path to Great Answers
coreMove: Push past the first adequate answer by searching seriously for the answer that changes the standard.
sourcePressure: Part 2 shifts from asking the question to finding stronger answers through serious search, while avoiding perfectionist delay.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Confusing great answers with endless research or perfectionist delay.

hook: A single choice changes the whole day
The real priority is hiding under the busy work
The Path to Great Answers as a generic focus opener
counterintuition: Focus is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: Set a timer and list priorities
Write down your one thing without a concrete context
examples: generic office worker choosing email or strategy

exampleSpecs.stakes: a teenager may quit running because of pain
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she rejects the standard padding fix and calls a Paralympic technician to benchmark a different socket fit
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a carbon-fiber socket on a bench beside a worn running blade

exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he moves beyond adding one ferry and studies three island systems to find the transfer pattern that actually cuts waits
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a ferry timetable covered with tide marks and clinic appointment times

exampleSpecs.stakes: white bloom is ruining holiday inventory
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she predicts a colder room is enough, then benchmarks a master batch log and discovers the cooling curve standard is higher
exampleSpecs.firstImage: chocolate bars streaked white beside a temperature curve printout

exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he refuses a polished report answer and interviews the best comparable program to find the intake moment they treat differently
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folding table with incident maps and three unanswered interview calls

exampleSpecs.stakes: only two seedlings survived the last trial
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she sees the adequate answer was more misting, while the great answer required comparing germination protocols from a specialist archive
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two surviving seedlings under a humidity dome with archive pages nearby

exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he goes past the first discount offer and studies a city paper that rebuilt membership around one civic data product
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a subscriber churn chart beside a clipped civic data newsletter

tryThisNowSpec: For one important question, write the obvious answer, then find one benchmark or person that proves a stronger answer is possible.
